Petitioner is arraigned as an accused in Crime No.389/2022 registered at Whitefield Police Station,
for the offence punishable under Section 420, 406, 468, 506 of Ipc.
2.
This petition is preferred un
der Section 438 of Cr.P.C., seeking anticipatory bail.

3. Heard the learned counsel for petitioner, learned High Court Government Pleader for respondent/State and perused the material on record.
4.

In the complaint lodged by one Shivapriya, she has alleged that she is a B.Sc graduate and while searching for a job, one Mr.Chandrashekar introduced her to the petitioner - Ramesh Rao.M.V, said to be working in one Blue Stream Company as an HR and he promised her to get a job and an IT project.

She has further alleged that on various occasions, in the guise of providing her job and IT project, petitioner received a total sum of NC: 2024:KHC:6542 Rs.22,00,000/- but failed to provide her a job or the project as promised.

It is also alleged that when she met him and asked to return the money, she was threatened by the petitioner saying that he will throw acid on her etc.
5.
Learned High Court Government Pleader has contended that there are materials to show that the complainant has paid a sum of Rs.22,00,000/- to the petitioner.

He contends that the petitioner has cheated the complainant with a promise of providing her a job and IT project and later when she demanded her money back, she was threatened with dire consequences etc.
He has contended that the investigation is under progress and therefore, the petitioner is required for custodial interrogation.
6. According to the complaint, she met the petitioner on 20.12.2021 who promised her a job and IT project.
Therefore, she borrowed money from her friends and relatives and deposited to the bank account of the accused on installment basis.
It is not NC: 2024:KHC:6542 forthcoming as to why such a huge amount of Rs.22,00,000/- was paid by the complainant to the petitioner for obtaining a job or IT project.
Even though it is alleged that the petitioner has cheated innocent persons like complainant there is no complaint lodged against the petitioner by any person.
The complainant has stated that since the petitioner had threatened her, she stopped contacting him for the past six months.

sentences.text: The petitioner claims to be innocent.
He has undertaken to cooperate with the investigation.
The offence alleged is not punishable with death or imprisonment for life.
The allegations made against the petitioner have to be established in due course.

Considering the entire facts and circumstances,
the petitioner can be granted the relief sought in this petition.

Hence, the following:
ORDER 1. Petition is allowed.

In the event of arrest of the petitioner in Crime No.389/2022 of Whitefield Police Station, he shall be released subject to following conditions:
a) He shall appear before the Investigation Officer within a period of one week from the date of receipt of a copy of this order and shall execute a personal bond in a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees One Lakh only) with two sureties for the likesum.
b) He shall furnish proof of his residential address and shall inform the Investigating Officer/Court, if there is any change in the address.
c) He shall make himself available for the purpose of investigation as and when required and shall co-operate with the investigation.
d) He shall not tamper with the prosecution witnesses either directly or indirectly.
e) He shall be regular in attending the Court proceedings.
NC: 2024:KHC:6542 f) He shall not indulge himself in any criminal activity.
